chalisa.cau1: First I bow my head at Sāī's feet. I tell the whole story of how Sāī of Śirḍī came. ॥1॥
chalisa.cau2: Who his mother and father are, no one has ever known. Where Sāī took birth has remained a question like a riddle. ॥2॥
chalisa.cau3: Some say he is Lord Rāmacandra of Ayodhyā; some say Sāī Bābā is Hanumān, son of the Wind. ॥3॥
chalisa.cau4: Some say Sāī is Śrī Gajānana, the embodiment of blessing; some say Sāī is Devakī's son, the enchanter of Gokula. ॥4॥
chalisa.cau5: Many devotees take him for Śiva and keep worshipping Bābā; some call him an incarnation of Datta and worship Sāī. ॥5॥
chalisa.cau6: Think of him as you will, but Sāī is the true God. Most merciful, the friend of the humble, he has given the gift of life to so many. ॥6॥
chalisa.cau7: I will tell you of an event many years ago. A fortunate man's wedding party had come to Śirḍī. ॥7॥
chalisa.cau8: With it had come a very beautiful boy. Having come, he settled there and made the town of Śirḍī holy. ॥8॥
chalisa.cau9: For many days he wandered about and begged for alms from door to door; and he showed such wonders as have become immortal in the world. ॥9॥
chalisa.cau10: As his age grew, so his renown grew. In every house of the town the praises of Sāī Bābā began to be sung. ॥10॥
chalisa.cau11: Then Sāī's name began to resound in every direction, to the ends of the horizon. To protect the humble and the afflicted remained Bābā's work. ॥11॥
chalisa.cau12: Whoever went to Bābā's feet and said: I am poor, on him his mercy fell, and the bonds of his sorrow were loosed. ॥12॥
chalisa.cau13: At times someone begged: Bābā, give me a child. Then Sāī would say: So be it, and grant him the boon. ॥13॥
chalisa.cau14: Seeing the plight of the humble and afflicted, Bābā himself would grieve. Śrī Sāī's heart was as vast as the ocean. ॥14॥
chalisa.cau15: A devotee came from Madras, a man of very great wealth. His goods and treasure were beyond measure; only he had no child. ॥15॥
chalisa.cau16: He began to entreat Sāīnātha: Bābā, have mercy on me. My boat is tossed by the storm: you alone, take it across. ॥16॥
chalisa.cau17: Without a lamp of the family, darkness has fallen on my house; so I have come, Bābā, to take refuge with you. ॥17॥
chalisa.cau18: Without a lamp of the family, the show of wealth is in vain. Today, Bābā, I have come to your refuge as a beggar. ॥18॥
chalisa.cau19: Grant me the gift of a son, and I will be in your debt all my life. I hope in no one else; my trust is in you alone. ॥19॥
chalisa.cau20: He entreated and pleaded much, laying his head at his feet. Then Bābā was pleased and gave the devotee this blessing: ॥20॥
chalisa.cau21: Allāh will do you good; may a son be born in your house. His grace will remain on you and on that child of yours. ॥21॥
chalisa.cau22: To this day no one has found the limit of Sāī's grace. Giving the man from Madras a jewel of a son, he blessed his world. ॥22॥
chalisa.cau23: Whoever worships with body and mind is saved in this world. Truth has nothing to fear from the flame; falsehood is always defeated. ॥23॥
chalisa.cau24: I am always in his keeping, and I will always be his servant. I have found a Lord such as Sāī: is that by itself a small hope? ॥24॥
chalisa.cau25: I too had such a day, when I could not get bread. Clothes on my body were far away; only a tiny loincloth was left. ॥25॥
chalisa.cau26: Even with a river before me, I remained as thirsty as ever. My evil days rained a forest fire down on me. ॥26॥
chalisa.cau27: Apart from the earth, I had no support in the world. Become a beggar in the world, I was knocked about from door to door. ॥27॥
chalisa.cau28: At such a time I met a friend who was a great devotee of Sāī. He was free of entanglements, but in the world he too was like me. ॥28॥
chalisa.cau29: For the sight of Bābā the two of us took counsel together, and we made ready for the darśana of Sāī, the embodiment of compassion. ॥29॥
chalisa.cau30: In the holy town of Śirḍī we saw that enrapturing form. Our birth was blessed when we saw the form of Sāī. ॥30॥
chalisa.cau31: Since we had his darśana, all our sorrow vanished like camphor. All our troubles were wiped away, and our misfortunes came to an end. ॥31॥
chalisa.cau32: Honour and respect, all of it, we received from Bābā as alms. By Sāī's command we came to shine in the world. ॥32॥
chalisa.cau33: Bābā has given me respect, has given me honour in this life. With this as my support I will go laughing through life. ॥33॥
chalisa.cau34: Sāī's wonders had such an effect on my mind that it seems as if he fills every particle of the world. ॥34॥
chalisa.cau35: Kāśīrāma, a devotee of Bābā, lived in this Śirḍī. He would tell the world: I am Sāī's, and Sāī is mine. ॥35॥
chalisa.cau36: He sewed clothes himself and sold them in the markets of villages and towns. The strings of his heart rang with Sāī's music. ॥36॥
chalisa.cau37: The night was still; the moon and stars slept in the lap of night. Because of the darkness, one could not see one's own hand. ॥37॥
chalisa.cau38: Alas, Kāśī was coming back from the market after selling his cloth. By a very strange chance, that day he was coming alone. ॥38॥
chalisa.cau39: Crooked wrongdoers surrounded him and stood in his way. The only cry to be heard was: Beat him, cut him down, rob him. ॥39॥
chalisa.cau40: Having robbed and beaten him, the crooks made off from there. Wounded to the core by the blows, he lost consciousness. ॥40॥
chalisa.cau41: For a long time he lay there in that state. Who knows when, in some moment, a little awareness came back to him. ॥41॥
chalisa.cau42: Unknowingly the name Sāī broke from his lips, and its echo reached Bābā's ears in Śirḍī. ॥42॥
chalisa.cau43: His mind was stirred, and Bābā was in anguish. It seemed as if the whole event had taken place before his eyes. ॥43॥
chalisa.cau44: Then Bābā began to wander here and there like one frenzied. Whatever things came before him, he began to fling down. ॥44॥
chalisa.cau45: And Bābā thrust his hand into the blazing coals. All who were there grew fearful, seeing this strange tāṇḍava dance. ॥45॥
chalisa.cau46: Everyone understood that some devotee had fallen into danger. All stood there troubled, lost in wonder. ॥46॥
chalisa.cau47: It is to save him that Bābā is in anguish today; his innermost heart suffers with that man's pain. ॥47॥
chalisa.cau48: Just then fate showed its strange ways, and seeing it, the people's river of faith surged. ॥48॥
chalisa.cau49: A cart arrived there carrying the unconscious devotee. Seeing the devotee before him, Sāī's eyes filled with tears. ॥49॥
chalisa.cau50: Bābā's innermost heart was calm, steady and deep like the ocean; yet today, who knows why, again and again it was stirred. ॥50॥
chalisa.cau51: Today the very embodiment of compassion had himself become the healer, and for the devotee's sake the god had become a doorkeeper. ॥51॥
chalisa.cau52: Today Kāśī had passed the hard test of devotion. Just to see him, the townspeople came thronging. ॥52॥
chalisa.cau53: Whenever and wherever a devotee falls into danger, Bābā goes in an instant to protect him. ॥53॥
chalisa.cau54: This is the truth of every age, no new story: when a devotee is in distress, the Indweller of all hearts goes himself. ॥54॥
chalisa.cau55: Beyond all distinctions, Sāī was a worshipper of humanity. Hindus and Muslims were as dear to him as Sikhs and Christians. ॥55॥
chalisa.cau56: Bābā broke down the division between temple and mosque. Rāma and Rahīm were all his, Kṛṣṇa, Karīm and Allāh Taʿālā. ॥56॥
chalisa.cau57: Every corner of the mosque rang with the echo of the bell. Hindus and Muslims met one another, and their love grew twofold day by day. ॥57॥
chalisa.cau58: What a beautiful miracle it was, such proof this body gave of itself; and Bābā filled even the bitterness of the neem with sweetness. ॥58॥
chalisa.cau59: Sāī gave affection to all and loved all with a love beyond compare. Whatever anyone wanted, Bābā gave him that. ॥59॥
chalisa.cau60: Whoever ever repeats the name of such a vessel of affection and goodness, even if his sorrow be like a mountain, it is removed in a moment. ॥60॥
chalisa.cau61: Ah, never has anyone seen a giver like Sāī, at the mere sight of whom all misfortune went away. ॥61॥
chalisa.cau62: Sāī in the body, Sāī in the mind: worship him, repeating Sāī, Sāī. Forgetting all awareness of your own body, keep him in your thoughts. ॥62॥
chalisa.cau63: When you let go of thoughts of yourself and keep Bābā in your thoughts, and night and day repeat Bābā, Bābā, Bābā alone, ॥63॥
chalisa.cau64: then, oh, Bābā will be bound to take care of you; Bābā will have to fulfil your every wish. ॥64॥
chalisa.cau65: Do not wander from forest to forest, foolish one, searching any further for Bābā. In one place only, in Śirḍī, will you find Bābā. ॥65॥
chalisa.cau66: Blessed in the world is the soul who has found Bābā, and in sorrow or in joy, through all the eight watches, has sung Sāī's praises alone. ॥66॥
chalisa.cau67: Let mountains of troubles fall, or lightning itself strike, always take Sāī's name and stand firm before all. ॥67॥
chalisa.cau68: Hear the wonder of this old man and you will be amazed; hearing it, who knows how many clever and wise were left astonished. ॥68॥
chalisa.cau69: Once a false sādhu came to Śirḍī. He had beguiled the simple people of the town. ॥69॥
chalisa.cau70: Showing them herbs, he began to make a speech there. He began to say: Listen, my audience: my home is Vṛndāvana. ॥70॥
chalisa.cau71: I have a medicine, and there is a wondrous power in it. Simply by taking it one is freed from sorrow. ॥71॥
chalisa.cau72: If you wish to be free of trouble and disease, then my humble request to every man and every woman is this: ॥72॥
chalisa.cau73: buy it; the ways of taking it are unique. Though it is a small thing, its virtues are very great. ॥73॥
chalisa.cau74: Whoever here is childless, if he takes my medicine, oh, he will have a jewel of a son and gain the fruit he asks for. ॥74॥
chalisa.cau75: Whoever does not buy my medicine will regret it all his life. Oh, someone like me will hardly ever come here again. ॥75॥
chalisa.cau76: The world is a fair of two days; you too, enjoy yourselves. If everything is gained from this, you too, take it. ॥76॥
chalisa.cau77: The people's wonder grew as they watched his tricks; and he too was delighted within, seeing the people's simplicity. ॥77॥
chalisa.cau78: A servant ran to give Bābā this news. Hearing it, his brows knitted, and all composure left him. ॥78॥
chalisa.cau79: He commanded the servant: Seize the scoundrel at once and bring him here, or drive the cheat away beyond the bounds of Śirḍī. ॥79॥
chalisa.cau80: While I am here, who is so base as to dare to deceive the simple people of Śirḍī? ॥80॥
chalisa.cau81: In a moment I will cast such a false, deceitful, base robber into the great pit of destruction for the rest of his life. ॥81॥
chalisa.cau82: The cruel, crooked, wicked juggler got a hint that death now danced over his head, that Sāī was angry. ॥82॥
chalisa.cau83: In a moment he shut down his whole show and ran for his life. He was thinking within: O God, is there no escape now? ॥83॥
chalisa.cau84: It is true: a giver like Sāī will not be found in the world. Sāī Bābā is a part of God; nothing in the world is hard for him. ॥84॥
chalisa.cau85: Whoever, wearing the ornaments of affection, good conduct, courtesy and the like, goes forward in this world on the path of service to humanity, ॥85॥
chalisa.cau86: he alone wins the innermost heart of every person in the world; a single sorrow of his moves the whole world. ॥86॥
chalisa.cau87: Whenever the burden of sin in the world grows heavier and heavier, he comes as an incarnation, only to remove it. ॥87॥
chalisa.cau88: Taking away all the sin and injustice of this world, he drives off the world's demon in a moment. ॥88॥
chalisa.cau89: A stream of the nectar of love begins to rain on the world, and people begin to embrace one another. ॥89॥
chalisa.cau90: Just so Sāī, an incarnation, came to the mortal world and, effacing his own self, taught everyone this lesson of equality. ॥90॥
chalisa.cau91: In Śirḍī Sāī named the mosque Dvārakā. With whatever he received, Sāī wiped away sin, suffering and anguish. ॥91॥
chalisa.cau92: Sāī would always sit absorbed in the remembrance of Rāma; through all the eight watches Sāī would repeat the name of Rāma. ॥92॥
chalisa.cau93: Dry or plain, fresh or stale, or even rich dishes: to Sāī, ever hungry for love, all were the same. ॥93॥
chalisa.cau94: Whatever people gave out of their affection and faith, Bābā would partake of that food with great relish and hallow it. ॥94॥
chalisa.cau95: Sometimes, to refresh his mind, Bābā would go into the garden, and gazing on the beauty of nature he would be glad at heart. ॥95॥
chalisa.cau96: The many-coloured flowers of the garden, gently swaying, filled even a rugged, desolate mind with the water of love. ॥96॥
chalisa.cau97: Even at such a sweet hour, people stricken by sorrow, misfortune and calamity would crowd around Bābā to tell the pain of their hearts. ॥97॥
chalisa.cau98: Hearing their sad stories, his lotus eyes would fill with tears; giving them vibhūti, he would take away every pain and fill their hearts with peace. ॥98॥
chalisa.cau99: Who knows what wondrous power was in that vibhūti: those who put it on their foreheads, it took away all their sorrow. ॥99॥
chalisa.cau100: Blessed are the people who had the sight of Bābā Sāī in person; blessed are their lotus hands, with which they touched his lotus feet. ॥100॥
chalisa.cau101: Nirbhaya, if only you too had met Sāī in person, our garden, laid waste for years, would bloom again today. ॥101॥
chalisa.cau102: Had I held the feet of Śrī Sāī, I would not have let go all my life; had Sāī been displeased with me, I would surely have won him back. ॥102॥
